Networking & Security: The Python MT5 Live Copilot (e.g., mt5_live_copilot_v1.99_beta.py) MUST be bound to 127.0.0.1 for ports 5555 and 5556 to prevent external exposure.

WINE Network Limitations: The MT5 EA MUST have a SocketConnect timeout of at least 2000ms during initialization because WINE's TCP stack requires time to construct the initial sockets under load. Short timeouts (1-50ms) will fail silently.

MT5 Terminal Permissions: The MT5 Terminal must have 'Allow DLL imports' and 'Allow WebRequest' enabled in Tools -> Options -> Expert Advisors, and the WebRequestUrl must contain http://127.0.0.1 and http://localhost. Otherwise SocketConnect fails with error 4014 (ERR_FUNCTION_NOT_ALLOWED). This can also be forced by editing Config/common.ini.

RAG Database: The RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) GUI knowledge base is located at /home/misi/LGBM_mlops/Knowledge_Base/External_Repos/. It contains an SQLite FTS5 database (gui_rag.db) with knowledge about lightweight-charts, TradingView API, Dash, etc.

HUD Status: The LAST FULLY WORKING PyQt5/Lightweight-Charts HUD script is HUD_Development/dual_hud_v1.51.py (it renders live ticks perfectly). All newer versions (v1.55, v1.56, v1.58) that attempt to read the 100 historical bars from history_init.csv fail to render candlesticks or prediction lines, crashing the JS engine ('Cannot read property series of undefined' / 'Value is null').

Heavyweight UI Success: The experimental TradingView Advanced Charting UI (tv_python_server.py) successfully loads the 100 historical bars and continues building candles, proving the data pipeline works. The issue is strictly isolated to the lightweight-charts-python wrapper's handling of DataFrames on subcharts.
